items.name: Non-positive K-groups of a connective ring spectrum
items.statement: Blumberg–Gepner–Tabuada [BGT13, Theorem 9.53]: for a connective ring spectrum R, K_i(R) ≅ K_i(π_0R) for all i ≤ 0, where π_0R is the discrete ring.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Corollary 4.7, p. 19, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. items.name: Weibel: NK_* is a Z[1/p]-module when p is invertible
items.statement: Weibel [Wei81]: for a discrete ring A in which p is invertible, p acts invertibly on NK_*(A), where NK(A) = fib(K(A[x]) → K(A)); hence NK(A)^∧_p = 0 and L_{K(1)}NK(A) = 0. This is the whole proof of Corollary 4.25 once A is reduced to a discrete ring with p invertible. The paper also cites [Wei81, Corollary 5.4] in Example 4.8 for the rational equivalence K(Z/p^kZ) ⊗ Q ≃ K(F_p) ⊗ Q.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Corollary 4.25, p. 23, and in Example 4.8, p. 19, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Weibel, Mayer–Vietoris sequences and module structures on NK_*, Lecture Notes in Math. 854 (1981), 466–493, and its Corollary 5.4)

items.name: Ravenel: complex-oriented rings of height at most n are L_n-local
items.statement: Ravenel [Rav84, Theorem 2.1]: BP[v_n^{−1}] has the Bousfield class of K(0) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ K(n) and is therefore L_n-local, where L_n = L_{K(0)⊕⋯⊕K(n)}. Consequently every p-local complex-oriented ring spectrum whose formal group law has height at most n is L_n-local, and so is every limit of such spectra; this is how the proof of Corollary 4.21 shows Tmf_(p) to be L_2-local.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Corollary 4.21, p. 22, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Ravenel, Localization with respect to certain periodic homology theories, Amer. J. Math. 106 (1984), Theorem 2.1)
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-LAND-MATHEW-MEIER-ETAL-24 (RT-PAPER-LAND-MATHEW-MEIER-ETAL-24/5(h)).

items.name: K(n)- and T(n)-localization agree on L_n-local spectra
items.statement: L_{n−1}-local spectra are T(n)-acyclic, because L_{n−1} is smashing (Hopkins–Ravenel) and T(n) is K(0) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ K(n−1)-acyclic. Consequently, for an L_n-local spectrum X, L_{T(n)}X ≃ L_{K(n)}X: the fibre of X → L_{K(n)}X is L_n-local and K(n)-acyclic, hence L_{n−1}-local and so T(n)-acyclic, while L_{K(n)}X is T(n)-local. The paper proves the second statement in-line.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 4.21, p. 22, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: TMF with level-3 structure and the K(2)-local Galois extension
items.statement: At p = 2, TMF_(2) → TMF(3)_(2) is a faithful GL_2(F_3)-Galois extension [MM15, Theorem 7.6]; it localizes to the Galois extension L_{K(2)}TMF → L_{K(2)}TMF(3) ≃ E_2, with E_2 the Lubin–Tate spectrum of a supersingular elliptic curve over F_4 [Beh20, Proposition 6.6.10; Heard–Mathew–Stojanoska, Proposition 3.6]. At p = 3, L_{K(2)}TMF ≃ E_2^{hG_24}, with E_2 the Lubin–Tate spectrum of a supersingular elliptic curve C over F_9 and G_24 its automorphism group over F_3.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Corollary 4.21(iv), p. 22, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Mathew–Meier, Affineness and chromatic homotopy theory, J. Topol. 8 (2015), Theorem 7.6; Behrens, Topological modular and automorphic forms, Handbook of Homotopy Theory (2020), Proposition 6.6.10)
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-LAND-MATHEW-MEIER-ETAL-24 (RT-PAPER-LAND-MATHEW-MEIER-ETAL-24/5(h)).

items.name: Galois descent for telescopically localized K-theory
items.statement: Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel [CMNN20, Theorem 5.6]: let A → B be a G-Galois extension of E_∞-rings with G finite, such that the image of the transfer K_0(B) ⊗ Q → K_0(A) ⊗ Q contains the unit. Then for every n ≥ 0 the maps L_n^fK(A) → L_n^f(K(B)^{hG}) → (L_n^fK(B))^{hG} are equivalences; in particular K(A) → K(B)^{hG} is a T(i)-local equivalence for every i ≥ 1. By [CMNN20, Corollary B.4] the transfer condition holds for E(𝔾,k)^{hH} → E(𝔾,k) with H a finite group of automorphisms of (𝔾,k); the paper applies this to L_{K(2)}TMF → E_2 to get K(L_{K(2)}TMF) ≃ K(E_2)^{hGL_2(F_3)} after every telescopic localization.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Corollary 4.21(iv), p. 22, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel, Descent in algebraic K-theory and a conjecture of Ausoni–Rognes, J. Eur. Math. Soc. 22 (2020), 1149–1200, Theorem 5.6 and Corollary B.4; read in arXiv:1606.03328v2)

items.name: The James splitting
items.statement: For a connected pointed space W, Σ^∞ΩΣW ≃ Σ^∞⋁_{k≥1}W^{∧k} (James; [Ada72, Chapter 10, Theorem 5]). In Corollary 4.14 it shows that Σ^∞ΩΣW is T(n) ⊕ T(n−1)-acyclic when Σ^∞W is.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Corollary 4.14, p. 20, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Adams, Algebraic topology — a student's guide, London Math. Soc. Lecture Note Ser. 4 (1972), Chapter 10, Theorem 5)

prerequisites.citation: Michael J. Hopkins and Jeffrey H. Smith, "Nilpotence and stable homotopy theory II", Ann. of Math. (2) 148 (1998), no. 1, 1–49
prerequisites.why: The periodicity theorem giving a v_n self-map on every type n complex, the thick subcategory theorem, and the nilpotence theorem (their Theorems 3, 7 and 11 and Corollary 3.8 are all cited by name). Everything in §2.1 rests on it: the existence of the telescopes T(n), the independence of their Bousfield class from the choice of (V_n, v_n), and Lemma 2.3's identification of K(n)- and T(n)-acyclicity for ring spectra.

prerequisites.citation: Andrew J. Blumberg, David Gepner and Gonçalo Tabuada, "A universal characterization of higher algebraic K-theory", Geom. Topol. 17 (2013), no. 2, 733–838
prerequisites.why: The source of §2.3: localizing invariants on Cat_∞^perf (§5), nonconnective K-theory (§9), the S_•-construction in the ∞-categorical form with S_n(𝒞) ≃ Fun(Δ^{n−1},𝒞) (§7.1), and the plus-construction description of τ_{≥1}K(A) for a connective ring spectrum (Lemma 9.39). These are the definitions in which every theorem of the paper is stated.

prerequisites.citation: Markus Land and Georg Tamme, "On the K-theory of pullbacks", Ann. of Math. (2) 190 (2019), no. 3, 877–930
prerequisites.why: The Main Theorem attaches to a pullback square of ring spectra a ring spectrum A' ⊗~_{A,B'} B making every localizing invariant take the square to a pullback, and Remark 1.16 computes the fibre. §3.2 is built on it: Lemma 3.2, Lemma 3.3 and hence Proposition 3.4. Their Lemma 2.4, Theorems 3.3 and A.2 and Corollary 3.5 — truncating invariants are nilinvariant and satisfy Milnor excision and cdh-descent — give Corollaries 3.5, 4.4, 4.16, 4.23 and 4.24.

prerequisites.citation: Dustin Clausen, Akhil Mathew, Niko Naumann and Justin Noel, "Descent and vanishing in chromatic algebraic K-theory via group actions", Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. (4), arXiv:2011.08233
prerequisites.why: Their Theorem C is Theorem 1.1 here, the second half of the Purity Theorem, and their Lemma 4.5 is the Tate-construction strengthening of Hahn's theorem. Their argument is summarised in Remark 3.9 and uses Theorem A of this paper but not the Purity Theorem; the two papers must therefore be planned in that order. Their Theorem A is Theorem B here, and they also proved Corollary 4.21(i).

prerequisites.citation: Jeremy Hahn, "On the Bousfield classes of H_∞-ring spectra", arXiv:1612.04386
prerequisites.why: A T(n)-acyclic E_∞-ring (indeed H_∞-ring) is T(n+1)-acyclic. This is what makes the height of an E_∞-ring well defined, and hence what turns Theorem A into the redshift inequality of Theorem B; it is also used directly in Corollary 4.3.

prerequisites.citation: Nicholas J. Kuhn, "Tate cohomology and periodic localization of polynomial functors", Invent. Math. 157 (2004), no. 2, 345–370
prerequisites.why: Blueshift for the Tate construction: it is what makes (L_n^{p,f}S)^{tC_p} an L_{n−1}^{p,f}S-algebra and so runs the induction of Remark 3.9.

prerequisites.citation: Nicholas J. Kuhn, "A guide to telescopic functors", Homology Homotopy Appl. 10 (2008), no. 3, 291–319
prerequisites.why: Theorem 1.1 is the Bousfield–Kuhn functor Φ_i with Φ_i ∘ Ω^∞ ≃ L_{T(i)}, the whole content of Proposition 2.9 that Σ^∞Ω^∞ detects T(i)-local equivalences, which is the mechanism by which the plus-construction argument of Proposition 3.1 sees the spectrum-level statement.

prerequisites.citation: Aldridge K. Bousfield, "On the telescopic homotopy theory of spaces", Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 353 (2001), no. 6, 2391–2426, with Tobias Barthel, Gijs Heuts and Lennart Meier, "A Whitehead theorem for periodic homotopy groups", Israel J. Math. 241 (2021), no. 1, 1–16
prerequisites.why: Bousfield's Corollary 4.8, in the form of Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 3.3 of Barthel–Heuts–Meier, gives the integer m of Proposition 2.11: an m-connective space with vanishing v_i-periodic homotopy for i ≤ n is T(i)-acyclic for i ≤ n. This is the connectivity bound N of Proposition 3.1 and therefore of the whole proof.

prerequisites.citation: Stephen A. Mitchell, "The Morava K-theory of algebraic K-theory spectra", K-Theory 3 (1990), no. 6, 607–626
prerequisites.why: L_{T(i)}K(Z) = 0 for i ≥ 2. It is the base of every induction in the paper: the second half of Theorem 3.8, the case n = 0 of Remark 3.9, the K(Z)-module argument in Proposition 3.12, and Remark 4.20.

prerequisites.citation: Bjørn Ian Dundas, Thomas G. Goodwillie and Randy McCarthy, "The local structure of algebraic K-theory", Algebra and Applications 18, Springer (2013)
prerequisites.why: Theorem VII.0.0.2, that K and TC agree relatively along a map of connective ring spectra which is a π_0-surjection with nilpotent kernel, gives Corollaries 4.5 and 4.30 and hence Corollary E; Theorem 5.3.5.1, the identification of stable K-theory with topological Hochschild homology, is what makes the optimality argument of Remark 3.11 work.

prerequisites.citation: Thomas Nikolaus and Peter Scholze, "On topological cyclic homology", Acta Math. 221 (2018), no. 2, 203–409
prerequisites.why: Theorems I.3.3(ii) and I.3.6 and an analogue of Lemma I.3.8(iii) identify the endomorphisms of R in the Verdier quotient Fun(BC_p,Perf(R))/Perf(R[C_p]) with R^{tC_p} and give that quotient a symmetric monoidal structure; this is the step of Remark 3.9 that lets Kuhn's blueshift be applied.

prerequisites.citation: Amnon Neeman, "The connection between the K-theory localization theorem of Thomason, Trobaugh and Yao and the smashing subcategories of Bousfield and Ravenel", Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. (4) 25 (1992), no. 5, 547–566
prerequisites.why: Theorem 2.1, the Thomason–Neeman localization theorem, produces the exact sequence 𝒞_{>n} → Perf(S) → Perf(L_n^{p,f}S) of Lemma 3.7 from the finiteness of L_n^{p,f}; tensoring it with Perf(A) is the reduction of the general case of Theorem A to the connective case.

prerequisites.citation: Clark Barwick, "On exact ∞-categories and the theorem of the heart", Compos. Math. 151 (2015), no. 11, 2160–2186
prerequisites.why: For a stable ∞-category with a bounded t-structure, K_{≥0}(𝒟) ≃ K_{≥0}(𝒟^♥). It is the engine of Proposition 3.12, Ishan Levy's alternative proof, together with Quillen's dévissage theorem for abelian categories and Mitchell's theorem.

prerequisites.citation: David Gepner, Moritz Groth and Thomas Nikolaus, "Universality of multiplicative infinite loop space machines", Algebr. Geom. Topol. 15 (2015), no. 6, 3107–3153
prerequisites.why: Group-completion K-theory K^add of a symmetric monoidal ∞-category, with the semiadditivity of Cat_∞^perf (their Definition 2.1). It is what the S_•-construction argument of Proposition 3.6 group-completes, and it is the left-hand side of Corollary 4.31.

prerequisites.citation: Allen Yuan, "Examples of chromatic redshift in algebraic K-theory", J. Eur. Math. Soc., arXiv:2111.10837, with Robert Burklund, Tomer M. Schlank and Allen Yuan, "The Chromatic Nullstellensatz", arXiv:2207.09929
prerequisites.why: The converse of Theorem B. Yuan proves hgt(K(E_n)) ≥ n+1 for Lubin–Tate theory using Theorem A of this paper, and the chromatic Nullstellensatz produces, for any E_∞-ring R with L_{T(n)}R ≠ 0, an E_∞-map R → E_n; together with Theorem B this is the Redshift Theorem. Yuan's examples are also what show in Remark 3.11 that purity is optimal.

prerequisites.citation: Mark Mahowald and Hal Sadofsky, "v_n telescopes and the Adams spectral sequence", Duke Math. J. 78 (1995), no. 1, 101–129
prerequisites.why: Their Lemma 2.1 is the argument for Lemma 2.2(vii), that the Bousfield class of T(n) is independent of the choice of (V_n,v_n), and their Proposition 3.3 is what makes every L_n^{p,f}-acyclic spectrum a colimit of finite ones in Lemma 2.6. Without these two the localizations L_n^{p,f} are not well behaved.

prerequisites.citation: Akhil Mathew and Lennart Meier, "Affineness and chromatic homotopy theory", J. Topol. 8 (2015), no. 2, 476–528
prerequisites.why: Global sections of quasi-coherent 𝒪^top-modules preserve colimits, and Theorem 7.6 is the faithful GL_2(F_3)-Galois extension TMF_{(2)} → TMF(3)_{(2)}. These are exactly what Corollary 4.21(iii) and (iv) need, together with the descent results of Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel.

prerequisites.citation: Andrew J. Blumberg and Michael A. Mandell, "The localization sequence for the algebraic K-theory of topological K-theory", Acta Math. 200 (2008), no. 2, 155–179, and Benjamin Antieau, David Gepner and Jeremiah Heller, "K-theoretic obstructions to bounded t-structures", Invent. Math. 216 (2019), no. 1, 241–300
prerequisites.why: Blumberg–Mandell's fibre sequence K^cn(Z) → K^cn(ku) → K^cn(KU) is the earlier, height-one case of Corollary 4.19 and the n = 1 case of Rognes's question in Remark 4.13; Antieau–Gepner–Heller's dévissage theorem (Proposition 4.4), with Barwick–Lawson's connective predecessor, gives the fibre sequence K(F_p) → K(k(m)) → K(K(m)) of Remark 4.10 and extends these localization sequences to nonconnective K-theory.

prerequisites.citation: Wolfgang Lück, Holger Reich, John Rognes and Marco Varisco, "Algebraic K-theory of group rings and the cyclotomic trace map", Adv. Math. 304 (2017), 930–1020, with Dustin Clausen, Akhil Mathew and Matthew Morrow, "K-theory and topological cyclic homology of henselian pairs", J. Amer. Math. Soc. 34 (2021), no. 2, 411–473
prerequisites.why: Their Theorem 1.19 gives the assembly equivalence for THH on the family of cyclic subgroups, and their §6 shows the non-p-completed TC statement fails; Clausen–Mathew–Morrow's Theorem 2.7 and Corollaries 2.15 and their Theorem G supply the colimit and finiteness properties of TC and TC/p. Together they give Proposition 4.33 and hence Corollary F, and Corollaries 4.32 and Remark 4.29.

prerequisites.citation: Shachar Carmeli, Tomer M. Schlank and Lior Yanovski, "Ambidexterity in T(n)-local stable homotopy theory", Invent. Math. 228 (2022), no. 3, 1145–1254
prerequisites.why: Their Theorem E, that for a p-local ring spectrum R the vanishing of R ⊗ K(π,r) for all r > i is equivalent to the vanishing of R ⊗ K(r) for all r > i, is what sharpens the connectivity bound of Proposition 2.11 to m = n+1 in Remark 2.12.

prerequisites.citation: Robert Burklund, Jeremy Hahn, Ishan Levy and Tomer M. Schlank, "K-theoretic counterexamples to Ravenel's telescope conjecture", arXiv:2310.17459
prerequisites.why: The telescope conjecture is false at every height above one and every prime. This is why the paper is careful to state everything for telescopes T(n) rather than Morava K-theories K(n), why Lemma 2.3 for ring spectra is a separate theorem, and why Question 3.10 — the K(n)-local analogue of purity — is open.

prerequisites.citation: Bhargav Bhatt, Dustin Clausen and Akhil Mathew, "Remarks on K(1)-local K-theory", Selecta Math. (N.S.) 26 (2020), no. 3, Paper No. 39
prerequisites.why: Their results for HZ-algebras — that a T(0)-equivalence induces an equivalence on K(1)-local K-theory, and that L_{T(1)}K(A[1/p]) ≃ L_{T(1)}TC(A) for a commutative p-adically complete ring — are the height-one shadow that Corollary C, Corollary 4.23 and Corollary 4.30 generalise to arbitrary ring spectra by purely homotopy-theoretic means.

prerequisites.citation: Dustin Clausen, Akhil Mathew, Niko Naumann and Justin Noel, "Descent in algebraic K-theory and a conjecture of Ausoni–Rognes", J. Eur. Math. Soc. (JEMS) 22 (2020), no. 4, 1149–1200
prerequisites.why: Theorem 5.6, Galois descent for L_n^f-localized K-theory along a G-Galois extension of E_∞-rings whose rationalized transfer hits the unit, and Corollary B.4, which verifies that condition for Lubin–Tate spectra, give the equivalence K(L_{K(2)}TMF) ≃ K(E_2)^{hGL_2(F_3)} after every telescopic localization in Corollary 4.21(iv). This is the paper's [CMNN20], distinct from the [CMNN23] listed above.

prerequisites.citation: Douglas C. Ravenel, "Localization with respect to certain periodic homology theories", Amer. J. Math. 106 (1984), no. 2, 351–414
prerequisites.why: Theorem 2.1, that BP[v_n^{−1}] has the Bousfield class of K(0) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ K(n), makes complex-oriented rings of height at most n L_n-local; this is how Corollary 4.21 shows Tmf_(p) to be L_2-local and hence T(n)-acyclic for n ≥ 3.

prerequisites.citation: Fabian Hebestreit and Wolfgang Steimle, "Stable moduli spaces of hermitian forms", arXiv:2103.13911
prerequisites.why: The stable envelope Stab(𝒞) of an additive ∞-category and the identification of τ_{≥0}K(Stab(𝒞)) with the group completion of 𝒞^≃ (Corollary 8.1.3 as the paper cites it), on which Ishan Levy's Proposition 3.12 is built.

prerequisites.citation: Irakli Patchkoria and Piotr Pstrągowski, "Adams spectral sequences and Franke's algebraicity conjecture", arXiv:2110.03669
prerequisites.why: Theorem 4.26 restricts the t-structure on Fun^add(𝒞^op, Sp) to the fibre 𝒟 of Proposition 3.12, which is what gives 𝒟 a bounded t-structure and lets the theorem of the heart apply.

prerequisites.citation: Lars Hesselholt and Thomas Nikolaus, "Topological cyclic homology", in Handbook of Homotopy Theory, CRC Press (2020), 619–656
prerequisites.why: Theorem 1.4.1, that the cofibre of the TC assembly map for C_p lies in the localizing subcategory generated by the coefficient ring, is the step of Remark 3.9 that makes the first map of the Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel argument a T(n+1)-local equivalence.

prerequisites.citation: Charles A. Weibel, "Mayer–Vietoris sequences and module structures on NK_*", in Algebraic K-theory, Evanston 1980, Lecture Notes in Math. 854, Springer (1981), 466–493
prerequisites.why: That NK_*(A) is a Z[1/p]-module when p is invertible in A is the whole proof of Corollary 4.25, homotopy invariance of K(1)-local K-theory; its Corollary 5.4 is used in Example 4.8.

prerequisites.citation: Mark Mahowald, Douglas Ravenel and Paul Shick, "The triple loop space approach to the telescope conjecture", in Homotopy methods in algebraic topology (Boulder, 1999), Contemp. Math. 271, Amer. Math. Soc. (2001), 217–284
prerequisites.why: Section 3 constructs the Thom spectra y(m) from the James filtration of ΩS^3 = ΩΣS^2, which §4.2 uses for Lemma 4.15 and Corollaries 4.16 and 4.18, and supplies π_0y(m) = F_p for odd p.

routes.title: General algebraic K-theory, Part II: telescopic localizations and the purity theorem
routes.brief:
Land-Mathew-Meier-Tamme prove that for any E_1-ring A and any n >= 1 the map A -> L_{T(n-1) + T(n)}A is an equivalence on T(n)-local K-theory: the T(n)-local K-theory of a ring spectrum sees only two adjacent chromatic heights. GeneralAlgebraicKTheory plans algebraic K-theory of exact and Waldhausen categories through the Q- and S-constructions, the fundamental theorems, the nonconnective extension and Morita invariance, and it plans no localization of K-theory at a Morava K-theory or a telescope; nothing anywhere in the atlas does. This Part II is where the chromatic behaviour of K-theory is planned, on top of the general theory its parent owns and the chromatic homotopy theory proposed alongside it.

Final theorems. Theorem A in its two halves and their common reformulation Theorem 3.8: A -> L_n^{p,f}A is an equivalence on L_{T(i)}K(-) for 1 <= i <= n, and for n >= 2 so is A -> L_{T(1) + ... + T(n)}A on L_{T(n)}K(-). The Purity Theorem itself, obtained from Theorem A and the Clausen-Mathew-Naumann-Noel vanishing of L_{T(n)}K(L_{n-2}^{p,f}S), whose argument Remark 3.9 reproduces and which uses Theorem A but not the Purity Theorem, so that there is no circularity. Theorem B, the redshift inequality hgt(K(R)) <= hgt(R)+1 for an E_infty-ring, and the Redshift Theorem hgt(K(R)) = hgt(R)+1 for hgt(R) >= 0 once Yuan's and Burklund-Schlank-Yuan's converse is imported. Proposition 3.1, the highly connective case, and Proposition 3.4, that L_{T(n)}K is truncating on L_n^{p,f}-acyclic ring spectra, with Lemma 3.3 reducing truncation to a single Postnikov stage. Proposition 3.6 and Lemma 3.7, the passage from connective to arbitrary ring spectra through the S_. construction and the Thomason-Neeman localization sequence. Proposition 3.12, Ishan Levy's second proof through a stable category with a bounded t-structure. Plan here, besides the first layer, the other cited inputs no layer plans: Weibel's theorem that NK_*(A) is a Z[1/p]-module when p is invertible in A, the whole proof of Corollary 4.25, and Clausen-Mathew-Naumann-Noel's Galois descent for telescopically localized K-theory (JEMS 2020, Theorem 5.6 and Corollary B.4), which Corollary 4.21(iv) uses. And the statements at height one and at heights at least two are genuinely different: Corollary 4.30 fails for n = 1, as the nonvanishing of L_{K(1)}TC(Z) against the vanishing of L_{K(1)}TC(Z[1/p]) shows.

routes.title: Chromatic homotopy theory: telescopes, Morava K-theories and finite localizations
routes.brief:
The atlas has no chromatic homotopy theory at all: a search of every layer description for Morava K-theory, Bousfield localization, telescopes, redshift, topological modular forms, the nilpotence theorem and ring spectra returns nothing, and no paper routed so far proposes a roadmap in this direction; but PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-21, merged a day before this extraction, routes chromatic basics to MotivicEtaleKTheoryPartIISelmerAndEtaleKTheory, a route its review rejected because generic chromatic spectra must come from their owning roadmap (see the paragraph on Clausen-Mathew below). Land-Mathew-Meier-Tamme's purity theorem is stated entirely in this language, and so are the theorems of Clausen-Mathew-Naumann-Noel, Hahn, Kuhn, Yuan and Burklund-Schlank-Yuan that it uses and feeds; the chromatic material is therefore planned once, here, and imported by the K-theoretic Part II proposed alongside it rather than re-planned there.

Final theorems. The periodicity theorem of Hopkins and Smith, giving a v_n self-map on every type n complex, with the thick subcategory theorem and the nilpotence theorem it rests on. The independence of the Bousfield class of T(n) from the choice of (V_n, v_n), and the characterisation of T(n)-acyclicity by the vanishing of v_n-periodic homotopy groups (Lemma 2.2 of the paper, all eight parts). The telescope conjecture for ring spectra: a ring spectrum is K(n)-acyclic if and only if it is T(n)-acyclic (Lemma 2.3), together with the record that the conjecture itself is a theorem at height one by Mahowald and Miller and is false at every greater height and every prime by Burklund-Hahn-Levy-Schlank. That L_n^f and L_n^{p,f} are finite, hence smashing, localizations, with the identification of their acyclics as Ind(C_{>n}) and the fracture squares of Lemmas 2.7 and 2.8. The Bousfield-Kuhn functor and its consequence that Sigma^infty Omega^infty detects T(i)-local equivalences (Proposition 2.9), and Bousfield's vanishing theorem giving that it preserves sufficiently connective L_n^{p,f}-equivalences (Proposition 2.11), with the sharpening m = n+1 from Carmeli-Schlank-Yanovski's ambidexterity criterion. Hahn's theorem that a T(n)-acyclic E_infty-ring is T(n+1)-acyclic, with the definition of the height of an E_infty-ring it makes possible and the Tate-construction strengthening used by Clausen-Mathew-Naumann-Noel. Kuhn's theorem [Kuh04]: for a finite group G and a T(n)-local spectrum X with G-action, L_{T(n)}(X^{tG}) = 0, equivalently the T(n)-local norm L_{T(n)}(X_{hG}) -> X^{hG} is an equivalence; in blueshift form, if X is L_n^{p,f}-local then X^{tC_p} is L_{n-1}^{p,f}-local, so (L_n^{p,f}S)^{tC_p} is an algebra over L_{n-1}^{p,f}S. The Tate construction itself need not vanish: (KU_p)^{tC_p} has pi_0 = Q_p(zeta_p), and the hypothesis that X is T(n)-local cannot be dropped, since S^{tC_p} is the p-completed sphere by the Segal conjecture for C_p. The cited inputs of the proofs, each an item: the Bousfield-Kuhn functor Phi_i with Phi_i Omega^infty = L_{T(i)} (Kuhn 2008, Theorem 1.1); Bousfield's theorem that highly connective spaces with vanishing v_i-periodic homotopy are T(i)-acyclic (Bousfield 2001, Corollary 4.8, with Barthel-Heuts-Meier); the Serre spectral sequence in T(i)-homology, and more generally in E-homology over an arbitrary base; Hopkins-Smith's nilpotence theorem, thick subcategory theorem and centrality of v_n self-maps (their Theorems 3, 7 and 11 and Corollary 3.8), with Mahowald-Sadofsky's Lemma 2.1 and Proposition 3.3 as the steps of Lemmas 2.2(vii) and 2.6; Ravenel's theorem that BP[v_n^{-1}] has the Bousfield class of K(0) + ... + K(n), so that complex-oriented rings of height at most n are L_n-local; that L_{n-1}-local spectra are T(n)-acyclic because L_n is smashing (Hopkins-Ravenel), and that K(n)- and T(n)-localization agree on L_n-local spectra; the James splitting of Sigma^infty Omega Sigma W; and, for tmf, the faithful GL_2(F_3)-Galois extension TMF_(2) -> TMF(3)_(2) (Mathew-Meier Theorem 7.6) with L_{K(2)}TMF(3) = E_2 at p = 2 and L_{K(2)}TMF = E_2^{hG_24} at p = 3.

Construct here, as the objects all of this is about: type n complexes and v_n self-maps; v_n-periodic homotopy groups of spaces and spectra; Morava K-theories K(n), connective Morava K-theory k(n), truncated Brown-Peterson spectra BP<n> and Johnson-Wilson theories E(n) with the fibre sequences relating them; telescopes T(n) with the convention T(0) = S[1/p]; Bousfield localization at a spectrum, Bousfield classes, smashing and finite localizations; L_1 = L_{KU}, L_n, L_n^f and L_n^{p,f} with the chromatic and telescopic filtrations; connective and periodic real topological K-theory ko and KO with the Bott element beta in pi_8 ko (the complex ku and KU are imported); formal groups of arbitrary height and their heights; Lubin-Tate theories E_n with their Morava stabilizer actions, through the Goerss-Hopkins-Miller theorem that E_n = E(k, G) is an E_infty-ring functorial in the pair (k, G), so that the automorphisms of (k, G) act on it by E_infty-maps; topological modular forms tmf, Tmf and TMF as the connective cover and the global sections of the sheaf O^top on the compactified moduli stack of generalized elliptic curves, through the Goerss-Hopkins-Miller-Lurie theorem constructing O^top as a sheaf of E_infty-rings on the etale site of that stack, as in Douglas-Francis-Henriques-Hill and Behrens, with the height bound on the formal groups of elliptic curves that makes Tmf L_2-local; Postnikov towers of spaces; and the Thom spectra y(m) and z(m) of the James-filtered maps into BGL_1(S^p), with Mahowald's and Hopkins's theorem identifying the colimit as HF_p.

Import, never re-plan: StableHomotopyKTheory H.5:spectra for a concrete model of spectra with suspension spectra, loops, shift, integer-graded stable homotopy groups and fibre sequences, and H.6 for mod-m coefficients, the Bockstein sequence, p-completion and the Milnor lim^1 sequence, which is what Lemma 2.2(v) and (vi) are about; EnhancedDerivedSheaves E0 and E5 for quasicategories, stable and symmetric monoidal infinity categories, Ind-completion and compact objects; RefinedTraceMethods RT.4:topological for complex topological K-theory ku and KU, the Bott class in pi_2 ku and Bott periodicity; Eilenberg-MacLane spectra from StableHomotopyKTheory H.5:spectra; from Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology) finite CW complexes and cofibrations (Stage 4), the ordinary homology Serre spectral sequence over a finite CW base (Stage 5) and Hurewicz and Whitehead (Stage 8); from Tau Ceti ModularCurves (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves) layer 7E (PD-5) the height of the formal group of an elliptic curve in the supersingular case, the one-dimensional formal group of height 2, unique up to isomorphism by Lazard's classification, citing tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.formalAdd for the formal group law of a Weierstrass curve. Plan here only the generalized-homology Serre spectral sequence over arbitrary bases and formal groups of arbitrary height. Mathlib has quasicategories and nothing else of this: no spectra, no smash product, no Bousfield localization, no Morava K-theory.

Two things must not be blurred. K(n)-acyclicity and T(n)-acyclicity are different conditions on a general spectrum and the telescope conjecture is now known to be false; every statement must say which one it uses, and Lemma 2.3 is what licenses passing between them for ring spectra. And L_n^{p,f} is not L_n^f: they differ at the bottom of the tower, agree on p-local spectra, and the p-local comparison is a lemma, not a convention.

One convention, fixed here for every consumer. T(0) = S[1/p], as in Land-Mathew-Meier-Tamme, and L_n^{p,f} = L_{T(0) + T(1) + ... + T(n)}; L_n^f is the localization at the p-local HQ + T(1) + ... + T(n), which is Clausen-Mathew's 'p-localization followed by finite localization away from a type-(n+1) complex', so the two L_n^f agree. Clausen-Mathew and Bousfield write T(0) = HQ; this roadmap writes HQ there. The Bousfield classes of S[1/p] and HQ differ (S[1/p] tensor S/l is nonzero for a prime l other than p) and agree on p-local spectra, and item /24 of this extraction, L_n^{p,f}X = L_n^fX for p-local X, is the comparison lemma. The telescopes T(n) are those of a fixed pair (V_n, v_n), whose Bousfield class does not depend on the choice.

Clausen-Mathew is a second source and consumer. PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-21 item /118 (L_1 = L_{KU}, L_{K(1)}, L_n^f, Morava K-theory and telescopes) is chromatic basics that this roadmap owns; that paper's route to MotivicEtaleKTheoryPartIISelmerAndEtaleKTheory was rejected by its review for exactly this reason, and its revision should import /118 from here. Its items /150 (L_n^f-localized noncommutative motives), /024 (K(1)-acyclic connective spectra) and /142 (finite etale descent for L_n^f-localized K-theory) are consumers: they stay with their K-theory or motivic owners, which import this roadmap.

StableHomotopyKTheory is not the owner: its summary says in as many words that it is a Part II to AlgebraicTopology supplying group completion, the plus construction and concrete spectra, and that it 'is not a demand for all of stable homotopy theory before K_0 can be calculated'. These notions - type n complexes, v_n self-maps, Morava K-theories, telescopes, Bousfield classes, the finite localizations L_n^f and L_n^{p,f}, the Bousfield-Kuhn functor, Hahn's theorem, Kuhn's blueshift, ko, tmf and Lubin-Tate theory - are general notions used far beyond this paper, so by PROTOCOL section 15 they are planned once, in a roadmap that owns them, rather than inside the K-theoretic Part II that consumes them. Corrected on 30 September 2026 by FIX-RT-PAPER-LAND-MATHEW-MEIER-ETAL-24 (RT-PAPER-LAND-MATHEW-MEIER-ETAL-24/3 and /8): the scan of other papers matched roadmap titles and layer text only. Three facts the paper uses are trace-method statements with no chromatic content. RT.2 plans THH with its circle action and cyclotomic structure and the homotopy orbit, homotopy fixed point and Tate constructions with their norm sequence; the Nikolaus-Scholze identification of the endomorphisms of R in the Verdier quotient Fun(BC_p, Perf(R))/Perf(R[C_p]) with R^{tC_p}, and the symmetric monoidal structure on that quotient, are exactly that material and are used in Remark 3.9. All three are general and are cited by name, so they are recorded as this paper's demand on those two layers rather than planned again.

Z.1 plans finitely generated projectives as direct summands of free modules, idempotent matrices and ring K_0 ('Prove the correspondence between idempotent matrices up to stabilised equivalence and projective isomorphism classes'), so lifting idempotents modulo a nilpotent ideal belongs there. The KTheoryLowDegrees--U.1 packet currently lists nilpotent-ideal invariance (Weibel II.2.2) as not a target of Z.1; its blueprint job, BP-KTheoryLowDegrees--U.1, is still pending, so a source route can still reach it.
